Suggestion: ideally Firebase would have simulated the billing change for a while and sent customers a few months of 'your bill soon will be $xxx' emails before switching.

Counterpoint on Google support: 'Their support has been extremely good in my experience, and I'm far from a premium customer. Email/phone support readily available. Loads of their engineers available over slack.'

The startup's real problem was that deployed clients hit a Firebase endpoint they couldn't control or update quickly. Their fix in later client versions was to put their own controllable serverless endpoints in front of Firebase.
Commenter recalls an automated script that hammered their endpoint as hard as possible just to drive up their bill: 'I had a Firebase charge of $1k.'

Shipping API keys in the client is standard for Firebase apps, and Google recommended it, calling the keys 'public by design'. Those same Google API keys can now authenticate to Gemini. Google quietly updated the Firebase docs to say Firebase keys should be used only for Firebase APIs.

Praise for Firebase security rules: they cleanly separate data retrieval/update logic from access policy. You can prototype on a happy path and add authorization later with confidence you aren't leaking data. However, developers often don't grasp these mechanisms at first.

Built a real-time whiteboarding app for teachers on the original Firebase over 10 years ago. 'It was so fast I was able to build basic collision physics of letter tiles and have their positions sync to multiple clients at once.'
Firebase is 'notorious for having an unintuitive lack of server-side query options when you start using it.'
Besides pricing, the other painful thing about Firebase is the storage rules. If you switch to another serverless setup, you have to reimplement them, which is 'an absolute pain.'

Huge Firebase fan: what makes it special is the glue. Account management and libraries come for free, and the tools work together seamlessly, so the 'boring' parts are handled and you can focus on the interesting work. It's scary that there are no proper alternatives.

Firebase user finds it invaluable: a generous free plan and limits, plus database, auth, hosting, Functions and the CLI. They run APIs in production solely on Firebase Functions with Firestore as the database.
Firebase documentation beyond the basics is limited. The only resources are their docs and YouTube channel, 'which can feel limited once you pass the get-started depth.'

Uses Firebase and finds it 'easy, useful and constantly improving (cloud functions etc.)', but 'their support, however, is a joke'. Only 5 one-on-one email support questions per year, and their Twitter handle doesn't respond.

The detail that amazed this commenter: there was no visibility of the issue in the reporting tools, so the customer couldn't see what was increasing the bill. Billed usage also 'includes failed attempts which are blocked by their security rules.'
Another team went from ~$25/mo to $1000-2000/mo with the pricing change. They also saw 3-4 downtime incidents of over an hour in two months, with no way to contact anyone except a web form.

Indie developer's workaround: they use the Firebase Database purely as a JSON store and avoid proprietary features, so they can export and switch providers easily. Maintaining a secure, high-availability DB themselves isn't feasible.

Explanation of the spike: the REST API usage didn't use TLS session resumption or keep-alive, so each poll renegotiated TLS. Firebase had been under-reporting usage and began counting it correctly, but without warning or helping the customer fix their code.

AngularFire is one of the most amazing things about Firebase, enough that this commenter built a business on it. Firebase 'really cares about the developer experience' and makes you excited about programming.
Request: Firebase lacks a count query, so counting children requires downloading all the data. Count is such an important feature.

Longtime user calls Firebase one of the best systems they've used in a long time and is excited about analytics and crash reporting. They want a deeper database query language or realtime export to Postgres for SQL analytics.
